articles.description: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (CAFC) on Monday affirmed a district court’s grant of summary judgment of noninfringement in favor of Lowe’s Home Centers, LLC in a patent dispute over light-emitting diode (LED) light fixtures. The CAFC also upheld a $25,000 sanction imposed on the patent owner’s attorney for violating a stipulated protective order and affirmed the district court’s denial of Lowe’s requests for attorney fees under 35 U.S.C. Section 285 and sanctions under 28 U.S.C. Section 1927. articles.title: The Fairphone 6 Plus is modular, repairable, and $100 off right now
articles.description: The Fairphone 6 Plus comes with 12 replaceable parts. | Photo: Dominic Preston / The Verge Unlike most smartphones, the Fairphone 6 Plus is designed for home repair, with easily replaceable parts that could help extend its lifespan well into the future. That makes its midrange price point easier to justify, especially now that it’s dropped to a new low of $552.49 (about $98 off) at Amazon as part of the retailer’s ongoing Black Friday sale. Fairphone 6 Plus Where to Buy: $649.99 $552.49 at Amazon (black) $649.99 $552.49 at Amazon (green) $649.99 $552.49 at Amazon (blue) The 6.3-inch Fairphone 6 Plus features 12 user-replaceable parts, including the battery, screen, USB-C port, and cameras, all of which you can swap out with the included screwdriver. Replacement parts are relatively affordable, too; a new battery costs $39.99, which helps offset its middling battery life and lack of wireless charging. It also comes with a five-year warranty and up to six Android OS upgrades, making it a good option if you want a phone you can keep using for years. Although repairability is its marquee feature, the 6 Plus is also a solid midrange Android device. Fairphone prioritizes ethically sourced materials, making it a strong choice for environmentally conscious buyers who don’t want to sacrifice performance. Its Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 processor handles everyday tasks well, and its cameras take decent photos, though they’re not quite on par with those of pricier phones. What’s more, it offers a clean, bloatware-free Android experience and modular back panels, which you can swap for optional accessories like a card holder or crossbody strap. Our own Allison Johnson particularly liked the phone’s dedicated switch for turning on customizable focus modes called Moments, which can simplify your homescreen and limit access to distracting apps — something we could all use a little less of. Read our full Fairphone 6 Plus review.
